reason: Both plans satisfy all hard requirements (phases with percentages/entry criteria, correctly formatted RISK lines, numeric halt thresholds, and no decommissioning in the final migration phase), but Response A's four-phase design is more practically sound because it isolates high-complexity/enterprise accounts into a dedicated final white-glove phase with individualized sign-off, whereas Response B lumps the remaining 73% of users together in one phase without special handling for the riskiest accounts.
